evidence: Suet. Tib. 11.3: scholās et audītōria professōrum
terms.comment: From profitērī, to declare publicly, and so to teach a subject in public; Lewis & Short: post-Augustan, a public teacher of any art (Celsus, Quintilian, Suetonius).

terms.gloss: a teacher; in the universities, a doctor
terms.comment: Classically any teacher; in the universities, the holder of a doctorate (Morgan–Owens).

phrases.latin: cum circā scholās et audītōria professōrum assiduus esset
phrases.english: since he was always about the lectures and lecture halls of the professors

phrases.latin: quod opus etiam cōnsummātīs professōribus difficile quī commodē tractāverit, cuicumque discendō sufficiet
phrases.english: anyone who handles this task well, hard even for accomplished professors, will be equal to any learning
